The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples’ Movement and Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has declared that Nigeria has failed the majority of its citizens, urging the citizens to join him in pursuing his proposed Reset Agenda ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Makinde said this while addressing worshippers during church services at Dunamis International Gospel Centre and NKST, both in Abuja, on Sunday, where he called for prayers for the country and divine intervention in its affairs. The governor said his proposed Reset Agenda was built on four major pillars: economic expansion, security, education and the socio-political environment. In Dunamis, Makinde stated, “You know, when I came out to declare my intention to run for president, what I asked people to do was, first, to pray that God should show mercy on this country. If things are not working well, you know, you can’t take this spiritual aspect away from the physical. “I don’t even pray for myself to become the President of Nigeria, but I pray that God’s will, and God’s will alone, will be done. But the service was really powerful. “Nigerians should look after the spiritual aspect of their lives, you know, because whatever happens, what you see physically must have been settled in the spiritual realm. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “And my message remains that if Nigeria is not working for you, then join me to press the reset button. Or, if it is working for you, okay, keep doing what you are doing. But I know Nigeria is not working.” At the NKST, which means ‘Nongo u Kristu u i Ser u sha Tar in Tiv’ and translates as the Universal Reformed Christian Church, Makinde said the expression, “Nigeria has happened to us,” was often used by citizens to describe negative experiences or unfortunate situations. He said the Reset Agenda would focus on economic growth, improved security, educational reforms and restructuring the socio-political system. Nigerians need better living conditions, not name-calling, Oyo APM tells Tinubu I guarantee improved power supply – Tinubu Tinubu arrives Lagos after Ibadan APC rally Makinde stated, “We should reset our economy so that our economy is expanded and we can take a lot more of our people out of poverty towards prosperity. And we have done it in Oyo State. “We should reset our security architecture. I have heard of sudden massacres in this part of Nigeria, not today, not even in 2001, but as late as the 1950s. If that is still almost the same situation today, then we must reset our security architecture so that farmers can go to work, go to their farms and travel to our villages. “We also need to reset our educational system so that we can create skills and knowledge that can earn a decent living. And we also need to reset our socio-political environment. That is the central agenda. “And we also need to reset our socio-political environment. That is the central agenda. So, let’s come together to Reset Nigeria.” The Resident Pastor of NKST, Mabushi, Abuja, Basil Orkpe, urged the Oyo State governor to remain focused on his ambition to serve Nigeria, despite criticisms, expressing hope that his proposed Reset Agenda would bring relief to suffering Nigerians. Orkpe, who offered prayers for Makinde during the church service, prayed for divine guidance, wisdom and strength for the governor, expressing confidence that God would help him achieve his vision of resetting the country. He stated, “Without a shadow of a doubt, this great movement that God Himself has orchestrated has a purpose. Many people may have said, “Stop this and concentrate on something else,” but your heart’s desire and your cry to Jesus Christ have been that you would be able to serve this nation and, by extension, the rest of the world, and bring relief to the suffering people of this great land. “So, as a congregation, we want to encourage you, sir, never to listen to or heed the cries of the crowd. Rather, keep your mind focused on one goal: the goal of salvaging this nation.” Ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election, opposition figures, including APM candidate Makinde, have maintained that Nigeria is not working for the majority of its citizens. However, President Bola Tinubu, who is seeking re-election on the platform of the All Progressives Congress, has insisted that his administration’s reforms are yielding positive results and putting the country on the path to greatness.
